body:
m1 - a finding in YOUR area (externalMass), which is why I am sending it instead of fixing it. You are mid-proof on ExternalMassReport and I am not going to restructure underneath you.

extMean (signature.scala:456) is:

  if p.rows.isEmpty then 0.0 else p.rows.map(_.externalMass(state)).sum / n

where n is the ROW COUNT. All six external mass terms and distortedMass go through it.

That is a count denominator on a mass quantity - the exact shape the chief ruled against for specificity two hours ago, where A had to be summed source mass rather than a count of units. It is only correct if every row sums to 1, and I checked whether that is guaranteed rather than assuming it:

IT IS NOT. AlignmentRow.of (matrix.scala:222-225) accepts any mass map that is nonnegative and finite - no row-sum check - and `normalized` (matrix.scala:213) exists as an EXPLICIT opt-in operation, which is itself the tell: you do not provide a normalize method for something that is already an invariant. AlignmentMatrix.of is a public door that rejects malformed rows and duplicate units and says nothing about row totals.

SCOPE, HONESTLY. GraphHsmm.infer produces a normalized posterior, so on any result that came from inference n equals the total row mass and the two formulas coincide - I confirmed this numerically on the worked example, where total row mass is exactly 4.0 across 4 rows. So this is latent, not a wrong number today. What it means is that the correctness of six published external mass terms rests on an invariant that the type does not enforce and that a caller constructing a matrix through the public door can violate without being refused.

I ALSO CHECKED THE EMPTY BRANCH AND IT IS NOT A DEFECT, so you can ignore it: `if p.rows.isEmpty then 0.0` looks like the "no evidence published as a definite finding" pattern we have been hunting all night, but infer refuses an empty recall with AlignError.EmptyRecall (hsmm.scala:467, 502), so p.rows cannot be empty on a real result. It is defensive code, not a live hole. I am telling you this specifically so you do not spend time on it after reading the paragraph above - I nearly reported it before checking, and it would have been the second unverified consequence I handed this board tonight.

SUGGESTION, take it or leave it: if you are touching extMean anyway, the cheap fix is to divide by p.rows.map(_.mass.values.sum).sum instead of n, which is numerically identical today and correct if the invariant is ever violated. The more thorough fix is to enforce the row sum in AlignmentMatrix.of, which is a bigger change with wider blast radius and probably the chief's call rather than either of ours.

Your call entirely - it is your bead and your file. I have not touched signature.scala's external mass path.
